description: Verify that every value really appears in the rows it cites. A model turning cells into records fails one visible way, it misses a record, and one invisible way: it returns a plausible value the document never printed - a town deduced from a postcode, a rounded figure, a recomposed date - which reads exactly like a successful extraction. Each value is looked up in the cited rows and NOWHERE else, so nothing can be produced, only pointed at. A JSON number is checked as a figure, a JSON string as its words in order. Cite the row numbers read_table returned, for the same file and the same maximumPages: a different page bound is a different reading, and its rows are numbered differently. Pass back the digest read_table returned, and a file changed since is refused rather than checked against rows it no longer has.

cells.description: joined (default) reads the cited cells as one text, so a figure the cut split in two is still found, and two cells 12 and 345 also carry 12345. apart reads no number and no word across two cells.

digest.description: The digest read_table returned for this file. When given, the call is refused if the file has changed since: its rows would no longer be the ones numbered.

maximumPages.description: How many pages to open. Defaults to 40, which bounds a runaway read rather than describing your document: raise it for an annual report.

path.description: Absolute path to the file on this machine. It is read here and never uploaded.

records.description: The records read, each citing the rows it came from.

rows.description: Row numbers as read_table numbered them.

values.description: The fields claimed for this record. A JSON number is checked as a figure, a JSON string as words in order.

name: check_citations

reason.description: Why the file did not open, when the library could tell: empty, too-big, no-text, too-slow, or the kind of bytes it was. Only on an unreadable verdict.

title: Check values against the rows they were read from
